title: A methodology for detecting the wound state sensing in terms of its colonization of pathogenic bacteria
author: Zhou, Yao, et al.
materials: 5(6)-Carboxyfluorescein was dissolved in HEPES buffer system at a concentration of 95 mM, which is a concentration above the threshold of concentration induced self-quenching. Serial dilutions of 5(6)-carboxyfluorescein solution were made (95 mM, 50 mM, 9 mM, 1 mM, 10−1 mM, 10−2 mM, 10−3 mM, 10−4 mM, 10−5 mM, 10−6 mM), diluted by HEPES buffer listed in Table 1. Each diluted solution (200 μL) was analyzed for fluorescence intensity with excitation at 485 nm and emission at 520 nm by using the Thermo Scientific Varioskan LUX Multimode Reader. The resultant figure was then plotted with fluorescence intensity versus various concentrations of carboxyfluorescein containing unquenched and quenched concentrations. The results are shown in Fig. 1. The HEPES buffer system for dissolving and diluting carboxyfluorescein is listed in Table 1, all the listed compounds were previously prepared in distilled water. steps.title: Prepare HEPES buffer system
steps.instruction: Dissolve the following reagents in distilled water to make the HEPES buffer: 119.2 mg HEPES, 29.2 mg NaCl, 511.5 mg NaOH, 14.2 mg EDTA. Adjust volume as needed to obtain a working buffer solution at room temperature.

steps.title: Make 95 mM carboxyfluorescein stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5(6)-carboxyfluorescein in the prepared HEPES buffer to a final concentration of 95 mM (use 1784.6 mg of the dye if preparing the same mass‑based stock). This concentration is above the self‑quenching threshold.

steps.title: Create serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Using the 95 mM stock, prepare the following concentrations by diluting with the same HEPES buffer: 95 mM, 50 mM, 9 mM, 1 mM, 10⁻¹ mM, 10⁻² mM, 10⁻³ mM, 10⁻⁴ mM, 10⁻⁵ mM, and 10⁻⁶ mM.

steps.title: Aliquot diluted solutions
steps.instruction: Pipette 200 µL of each diluted solution into separate wells or cuvettes suitable for fluorescence measurement.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence intensity
steps.instruction: Using a Thermo Scientific Varioskan LUX Multimode Reader set at room temperature, record fluorescence for each sample with excitation at 485 nm and emission at 520 nm.

steps.title: Analyze self‑quenching behavior
steps.instruction: Plot fluorescence intensity versus carboxyfluorescein concentration. Identify the concentration at which intensity sharply decreases (self‑quenching begins above ~9 mM). Note that a quenched concentration of 50 mM is commonly used and that diluting this 10⁵‑fold restores fluorescence.
